title: External data acquisition and negative result (LIDC-IDRI)
question: Does adding 927 labelled slices from a second, higher-quality dataset improve performance on the original domain?
answer: No - it made performance significantly worse.

acquired.source: LIDC-IDRI via the TCIA public NBIA API

label_policy: LIDC malignancy is a 1-5 radiologist impression from up to 4 readers, NOT pathology-confirmed. Annotations of the same nodule were clustered in 3D and ratings averaged: mean < 3 benign, mean > 3 malignant, mean == 3 excluded entirely. No normal slices were taken from LIDC.
design: LIDC entered the TRAIN split only. Validation and test remained byte-identical and 100% IQ-OTH, so results stay directly comparable to the pre-LIDC numbers and a dataset shortcut cannot inflate them.

dataset_identity_probe.interpretation: Source is trivially separable (LIDC has a circular field of view), so the shortcut was fully available to the model.

mitigation_attempted: Two-stage transfer - pretrain on the merged multi-domain set, then fine-tune on IQ-OTH only at 0.3x learning rate - recovered part of the loss (F1 0.804 to 0.828, benign recall 0.60 to 0.73) but stayed significantly below baseline.
one_genuine_benefit: With the cost-sensitive decision policy applied, the LIDC-trained CNN reached benign recall 1.000 with ZERO missed findings (baseline 0.933, 1 missed) - but with normal recall 0.667 and no macro-F1 gain (p = 0.80), so it did not justify deployment.
decision: The deployed model is unchanged: EfficientNet-B3 to Quantum_4q, trained on IQ-OTH only. All LIDC artefacts and metrics are retained, because the negative result is itself a finding.
lesson: More data is not automatically better data. 927 slices from a higher-quality source - true DICOM, real Hounsfield Units, genuine patient IDs, 4-reader consensus - made a single-domain model measurably worse, because the domain gap outweighed the extra examples. Freezing validation and test as pure target-domain data is what made that measurement trustworthy.
what_would_be_needed: Domain adaptation (appearance/histogram matching or adversarial domain confusion), sourcing normal slices for the external domain so the classes are not domain-correlated, or enough external data to learn a genuinely domain-invariant representation.
